mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the discount rate for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.2%, or the Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 8.0% signals labor market slack that suppresses wage growth and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 8.0%, or the Rank IC between UNRATE and 5-day returns is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals a broad-based demand slowdown that triggers equity sell-offs, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline by more than 1% from their 3-month moving averages, or the interaction term in a regression of 60-day returns on HOUST and RSAFS is not statistically significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a manufacturing supply expansion regime (INDPRO above 100), rising industrial production indicates strong economic activity that supports corporate earnings growth, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO exceeds 100, or the Rank IC between INDPRO and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, or the Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of employment (PAYEMS above 130,000 thousand) indicates a strong labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS exceeds 130,000, or the Rank IC between PAYEMS and 5-day returns is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A strong GDP growth rate (GDPC1 above 2.0% annualized) signals robust economic expansion that supports corporate earnings, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.0% annualized, or the Rank IC between GDPC1 and 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and high unemployment (UNRATE) signals a severe economic downturn that triggers risk-off sentiment, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.2% and UNRATE exceeds 8.0%, or the interaction term in a regression of 20-day returns on FEDFUNDS and UNRATE is not statistically significant (p>0.05).
